/recording.from: Recording captures 30 frames per second by default, which is enough for scrolling, hover states, and CSS transitions to read as motion rather than as a slideshow. Use `--fps` to change it:
/recording.to: `--fps` controls the output playback rate (30 by default, 1 to 60 allowed), not the rate at which Chrome supplies new images. Capture is repaint-driven and may be sparse. Requesting 60 fps cannot prove smoothness or the presence of intermediate states.

/recording.from: # 60 fps for a short, motion-heavy take
/recording.to: # Request a higher output rate; inspect capture evidence separately

/recording.from: Valid rates are 1 to 60. The latest Chrome frame is held between repaints so the file duration matches wall clock.
/recording.to: The recorder seeds an initial screenshot and repeats the latest image between repaints. It catches up after short encoder stalls and fails if capture or encoding falls too far behind, rather than silently shortening the timeline. Playback duration and output FPS do not establish how much motion was captured.
